items.title: ChatGPT becomes first AI chatbot to face tougher EU rules
items.summary: BRUSSELS: ChatGPT will have to comply with tougher safety rules after the EU added it Monday to a list of digital services subject to greater legal scrutiny, a first for an AI chatbot. Brussels also designated Reddit and Roblox as "very large" online platforms, a label that comes with additional obligations and oversight. The "very large" designation applies to platforms and search engines with more than 45 million monthly active users in the 27-nation bloc, a threshold ChatGPT, Reddit and Roblox reported meeting, the commission said.

items.title: Malaysia seeks Nepal's nod to deploy Smart team for rescue operations
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has sought permission from the Nepalese government to deploy the Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (Smart) to assist in search and rescue (SAR) operations following floods and landslides in the country. "The discussion focused on the latest developments in the SAR operations, particularly efforts to locate Malaysians who remain uncontactable following the floods and landslides in Nepal recently," Mohamad wrote on his official Facebook page. On Sunday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim was reported as saying that the Madani government had decided to send the Smart team t o Nepal to assist in SAR operations following the floods that hit the country.

items.title: Muhyiddin backs cost-of-living measures, seeks broader relief in 2027 Budget
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin has welcomed the government's latest measures to ease cost-of-living pressures and support businesses, but called for broader relief under the 2027 Budget. "I welcome the Prime Minister's announcement of measures to ease the people's cost-of-living burden, assist businesses and strengthen government service delivery," he said in a statement today. He said the additional assistance was particularly important for businesses facing rising operating costs.

items.title: Malaysia seeks Nepal’s nod to deploy SMART team for flood SAR mission, says Tok Mat
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — Malaysia has sought permission from the Nepalese government to deploy the Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART) to assist in search and rescue (SAR) operations following the floods in the country. “The discussion focused on the latest developments in the SAR operations, particularly efforts to locate Malaysians who remain uncontactable following the floods and landslides in Nepal recently,” Mohamad wrote on his official Facebook page. On Sunday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim was reported as saying that the Madani Government has decided to send the SMART Team to Nepal to assist with SAR operations following the flood disaster that hit the country.

items.title: Spanish PM blames Russia, Israel for disinformation in Ceuta migrant crisis
items.summary: MADRID: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said on Monday there were signs Russia and Israel had spread the disinformation over Spain's migration policy that triggered last month's rush of migrants into Ceuta, but no evidence of Moroccan involvement. At least 100 people died in the attempt, according to Ceuta's local authorities. Videos on Instagram, TikTok and other social media spread misleading claims that migrants reaching Ceuta by sea could remain in Spain, encouraging thousands to attempt the crossing, Spanish authorities have said.

items.title: MAHA 2026 attracts 1.8 million visitors, records RM6m sales in three days
items.summary: SERDANG, Aug 31 — The Malaysia Agriculture, Horticulture and Agrotourism Exhibition (MAHA) 2026 has recorded 1.8 million visitors and nearly RM6 million in sales in its first three days, says Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu. He said 184,000 vehicles were recorded entering and leaving the exhibition grounds during the period, reflecting heavy traffic due to the large turnout. “Three days have passed, and visitor turnout for MAHA has reached 1.8 million, with 184,000 vehicles moving in and out.

items.title: Three-year-old boy injured after foot run over by tow vehicle at Terengganu National Day parade
items.summary: The boy’s mother, Puteri Anis Athirah Wan Rosli, 36, from Cendering, said the incident occurred at about 9.45 am in front of Wisma Persekutuan here. She said her son, Che Ku Muhammad Khairul Amir Che Ku Mohd Khairul Azlan, fell before being run over by the tow vehicle carrying a Fire and Rescue Department boat. My son followed her.

items.title: Veterinary Services Department recognises 167 artificial insemination technicians nationwide
items.summary: SERDANG: The Veterinary Services Department (DVS) today recognised 167 artificial insemination technicians nationwide for their commitment to strengthening livestock breeding services at the field level. He said the assessment also took into account artificial insemination service achievements, including the number of livestock receiving the service, the number of offspring born through artificial insemination and the number of livestock successfully impregnated through the procedure. "This award presentation is an important platform to appreciate the high commitment of artificial insemination technicians who are the frontliners in driving the genetic transformation of the country's livestock," he said in his speech at the Award and Appreciation Presentation Ceremony for Artificial Insemination Technicians and Livestock Farmers and the launch of the Artificial Insemination Management System (AIMS) here.

items.title: Beyond Merdeka: Building strategic resilience in a volatile world
items.summary: Today, however, threats to independence come through economic dependency, energy insecurity, disrupted supply chains, technological dependence and geopolitical conflicts taking place thousands of kilometres away. The current conflict in the Middle East, for example, affect countries far beyond the battlefield. Oil prices rise overnight.

items.title: AI programme to equip 100,000 youths for changing job market, says HR minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — The AI for the People Programme, which targets 100,000 youths aged between 18 and 30, is an important step towards preparing Malaysia’s workforce for rapid changes in the employment landscape, said Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan. He said access to artificial intelligence (AI) technology should be expanded among youth to ensure they possessed skills relevant to the needs of the current job market and were not left behind in global technologicl developments. “As such, providing 100,000 youths with access to AI technology is an important investment to equip Malaysian talent with relevant skills and ensure they are not left behind in the changing global job landscape,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Armizan: Political maturity key to keeping unity govt stable
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — Political maturity and the awareness of balancing political rights with the responsibility of nation-building are important to ensure the stability of the Unity Government, said Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali. In a Facebook post in conjunction with National Day today, he said the new political landscape of the country after the 15th General Election (GE15) needs to be accepted with the awareness that government stability is crucial in steering the direction of national development and the welfare of the people. He said the country’s new political landscape after the end of one-party dominance must be accepted by taking lessons from the experience between 2018 and 2022 which saw the change of three prime ministers and three Cabinet line-ups in one term.

items.title: BN strategy for Melaka polls must reflect grassroots wishes, component party leaders said
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Two Barisan Nasional component party leaders said the coalition must make decisions that closely reflect the wishes of its grassroots in determining its strategy for the Melaka election. MIC president Tan Sri S.A. Vigneswaran said the approach was important to ensure BN continued to lead Melaka. "All BN component parties are given room to put forward proposals, and after that we will take the best views," he said.

items.title: Tighter controls, stronger finances behind Budi Madani fuel quota restoration
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Improved supply management, stricter enforcement and the government's sound fiscal position were key factors in the restoration of Budi Madani fuel quotas from 200 to 300 litres. The Finance Ministry said the reinstatement of the monthly quota would take effect automatically for Budi Madani Ron95 (Budi95) and Budi Madani Diesel from tomorrow. Eligible owners of private diesel pickup trucks and four-wheel-drive vehicles may apply for an additional 100 litres per month, bringing their total monthly entitlement to 400 litres.

items.title: Haze: Serian, Kuching, Samarahan, Sri Aman record hazardous API readings at 5pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Sarawak's air quality continued to worsen, with four monitoring stations recording hazardous Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 5pm today. Eleven areas recorded "unhealthy" readings. Outside Sarawak, Labuan recorded an API reading of 165, while three areas in Sabah also recorded "unhealthy" readings.

items.title: South Korea court gives Unification Church leader two years in prison
items.summary: SEOUL: A South Korean court sentenced the leader of the secretive and powerful Unification Church on Monday to two years in prison on charges of bribing officials, including the wife of the then president. In a statement to AFP, the church vowed to appeal, saying it disagreed with the court's ruling. Han, revered by church members as the "True Mother", took the helm of the church after Moon's death in 2012.

items.title: National Unity Ministry remains committed to strengthening national unity, social harmony
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government, through the National Unity Ministry, remains committed to strengthening unity and social harmony in line with the National Unity Policy. National Unity Ministry secretary-general Datuk Haslina Abdul Hamid said this was being pursued through various programmes and initiatives aimed at strengthening social integration, fostering patriotism and building a more inclusive society. "This will ensure that the country's development and administration can continue in an atmosphere of peace and harmony," she said when met at the 2026 Anak Merdeka Malaysia celebrations here today.

items.title: King Charles conveys National Day message to Sultan Ibrahim, praises partnership and shared Commonwealth values
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — King Charles III and Queen Camilla have conveyed their congratulations to His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, and the people of Malaysia on the country’s National Day on Monday. In the message shared by the British High Commission in Malaysia, King Charles expressed confidence that the UK-Malaysia Strategic Partnership would provide a valuable opportunity to deepen cooperation between the two countries in trade, technology and other shared priorities ahead of the 70th anniversary of diplomatic relations in 2027. Meanwhile, King Charles also reflected upon the enduring partnership between the two nations, rooted in the shared values and mutual respect that define the Commonwealth.

items.title: Sabah CM Hajiji announces RM3,000 aid for each household hit by Kota Kinabalu fire
items.summary: Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor said the amount comprised RM1,000 contributions each from the state government, the federal government and the Yayasan Kebajikan Sabah. He said the state government would also assist efforts to rebuild the victims’ homes through coordination between the State Secretary’s Office and Majlis Amanah Rakyat (MARA). Hajiji said that on humanitarian grounds, each non-Malaysian KIR affected by the fire in the village would also receive RM1,000 in aid from the state government.

items.title: Indonesia probes citizens alleged to have fought for Russia in Ukraine
items.summary: JAKARTA: Indonesia said on Monday it was investigating claims that "several" citizens had joined the Russian military and were deployed in the war in Ukraine. The information, which came from Ukrainian authorities, was being verified with several ministries and government institutions, the foreign ministry in Jakarta said in a statement. "Information regarding the identity, citizenship status, recruitment process, and form of involvement of the individuals mentioned still needs to be further confirmed," the foreign ministry said.

items.title: Born on National Day, Malaysia Day: A birthday like no other
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: For some Malaysian families, Aug 31 and Sept 16 are more than dates on the national calendar - they are birthdays, too. Asked how they felt about sharing their birthdays with the country's celebrations, the boys said they were happy. "We are very happy to celebrate our birthdays with fireworks every year," they said.

items.title: Tunku Azizah Hospital welcomes 12 Merdeka babies
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: As the nation celebrated its 69th National Day, 12 newborns, including a pair of twin girls, began their life stories at the Tunku Azizah Hospital (HTA) today. All ten 'Merdeka babies' were delivered between midnight and noon, comprising six baby boys and six baby girls. HTA director Dr Shamsul Anuar Kamarudin said a birth on National Day is not only a special date, but it also carries a deeper meaning as a symbol of life, hope and the nation's future.

items.title: 'Serpent' Netanyahu tricks US into war: Iran FM
items.summary: TEHERAN: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on Monday called Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu a "serpent", accusing him of tricking Washington into going to war with the Islamic republic. "In Hebrew, Netanyahu openly crows that he suckered the US Administration into a war on Iran on behalf of Israel. Iran retaliated with attacks across the region as the conflict continued to spread.

items.title: Family prays for Gelugor hiker missing in Nepal floods, Penang government ready to assist
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 31 — The family of Muhammad Muhaimin Azhad Noor Hadi, who has reportedly remained unreachable following flash floods and landslides in the Nepal-Tibet border area in Nepal last Wednesday, hopes that the hiker will be found safe. He said the family, who live in Taman Tun Sardon, Gelugor, here, were currently in Kuala Lumpur to follow developments concerning Muhammad Muhaimin Azhad, who works with the Implementation Coordination Unit of the Prime Minister’s Department (ICU JPM) Penang, through Wisma Putra. “Yesterday, family members attended a meeting with Wisma Putra to obtain information about Muhammad Muhaimin Azhad, and until now, we have also not received any phone calls or messages from him in Nepal.

items.title: AEON Bank rolls out Merdeka Bonus campaign to drive digital payments
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: AEON Bank Malaysia has rolled out its Merdeka Bonus campaign in conjunction with Merdeka and Malaysia Day 2026, offering rewards to customers while encouraging wider adoption of digital payments. The digital bank said the six-week campaign was designed to reward customers while encouraging more consumers to embrace the convenience of digital payments for their daily transactions. AEON Bank said this year's campaign also reflected its commitment to making digital banking more engaging and intuitive for Malaysians, particularly students, working professionals and the wider community.

items.title: Israel signs three-billion-euro arms export deal with Greece
items.summary: JERUSALEM: Israel's Defence Ministry announced Monday it had signed a deal with Athens worth approximately three billion euros to set up an "Achilles Shield" aerial defence system for Greece. "Under the deal, Israel will build Greece a comprehensive, multi-layered air defence array, drawing entirely on Israeli-made systems and on the extensive operational experience Israel's defence establishment has gained during the war," the ministry said in a statement. It added that "this is the largest defence export deal in the history of Israel-Greece relations, and one of the largest in the history of the State of Israel".

items.title: Over 4,800 foreigners inspected in 334 ops in Terengganu
items.summary: Its director, Mohd Yusri Mohd Nor, stated that out of that number, 1,257 illegal immigrants were detained for various immigration offences. He said that 317 more were detained for overstaying under Section 15(4) of the Immigration Act 1959/6, while 372 people were detained for misuse of passes under Regulation 39(b) of the Immigration Regulations. He said the Terengganu Immigration also opened 207 investigation papers related to immigration offences during that period, while RM2.887 million in fines were collected.

items.title: Oil palm entrepreneur loses nearly RM250,000 to bogus investment scheme on TikTok
items.summary: TANGKAK: A 56-year-old oil palm entrepreneur's hopes of making high returns within a short period were dashed after she lost nearly RM250,000 to a bogus investment syndicate. District police chief Superintendent Roslan Mohd Talib said the suspect lured the victim by offering high returns if she joined the investment scheme. Roslan said the victim subsequently lodged a report at the Tangkak district police headquarters.

items.title: In London, son's agonising wait for news of parents missing in Nepal-Tibet floods
items.summary: SINCE a catastrophic flood struck the border area between Nepal and Tibet, Prajval Haldia in London has had no word from his parents who were on a pilgrimage in the region at the time. "We get a call every day from a foreign office, but they don't really have any news," Haldia told AFP on Saturday. Haldia described checking where his parents were located.

items.title: Maha draws over a million visitors, nearly RM6mil in sales
items.summary: SERDANG: More than one million people have visited the Malaysia Agriculture, Horticulture and Agrotourism Exhibition (Maha) 2026 in its first three days, generating nearly RM6 million in sales. Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu said the massive turnout also saw about 184,000 vehicles enter and leave the Malaysia Agro Exposition Park Serdang (Maeps). Mohamad, commonly known as Mat Sabu, said sales were expected to pick up towards the end of the exhibition, when visitors typically make larger purchases, particularly of plant seeds.

items.title: Car bomb in front of Mexico police station wounds seven
items.summary: ZACATECAS: A car bomb exploded in front of a police station in Mexico overnight Sunday, wounding seven people, authorities said. The blast happened in Ojocaliente in the state of Zacatecas, where Mexico's two largest drug cartels are fighting for control of key drug-trafficking routes. One police officer was also wounded in the blast, which damaged 13 vehicles, including two police patrol cars, he said.

items.title: At 101, Dr M attends National Day celebration in Putrajaya
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad attended the 2026 National Day celebrations at Dataran Putrajaya today in an electric wheelchair. Dr Mahathir later shared a brief National Day message on Facebook, accompanied by a video recounting his two terms as prime minister. "Happy Independence Day and 69th National Day, Malaysia," he said.

items.title: Moung Sinabung erupts, spews ash 3.5km above summit
items.summary: JAKARTA: Mount Sinabung in Indonesia's North Sumatra province erupted on Monday morning, spewing a thick column of volcanic ash about 3.5 kilometres above its summit. The Centre for Volcanology and Geological Hazard Mitigation (PVMBG) said the eruption began at 10.17 am local time with the thick, black ash column observed moving east and southeast. Mount Sinabung, located in Karo Regency, remains at Level II (Alert), while residents living near rivers originating from the volcano were advised to remain vigilant against possible volcanic mudflows.

items.title: Laman Padi enters Malaysia Book of Records with largest padi artwork
items.summary: SERDANG: A 2.83ha (7acre) padi showcase at Maha 2026 has earned a place in The Malaysia Book of Records for its record-setting work of art. Launched by Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu today, Laman Padi showcases Malaysia's padi and rice ecosystem at the Malaysia Agriculture, Horticulture and Agrodiversity Exhibition (Maha) 2026. Its centrepiece is a 119ft by 126ft (36.27m by 38.4m) padi art installation, recognised by The Malaysia Book of Records as the country's largest padi art formation.

items.title: Driver killed after container lorry plunges into 20m ravine
items.summary: GUA MUSANG: A man was killed after the container lorry he was driving skidded and plunged into a 20-metre-deep ravine along the Gua Musang-Kuala Krai road near Ladang Serasa here today. Gua Musang Fire and Rescue station chief Muhammad Azrul Izzham Zulkifli said the department received an emergency call at 9.11am on the incident. He said a team of seven firefighters in three fire engines arrived at the scene at 9.58am, about 65km from the station.

items.title: Nepal toll surges as rescuers struggle through 'unimaginable' disaster
items.summary: NUWAKOT: Rescuers struggled Monday through mud and debris for a sixth day, as the number of missing people soared to nearly 5,000 since tsunami-like glacial floods roared down from the China-Nepal border, creating an "unimaginable" disaster. The huge wave of freezing water, rocks and debris that smashed into villages and towns on Wednesday killed at least 903 people in Nepal and in Tibet, in China, with at least 17 bodies pulled from rivers downstream in India. Late Sunday Nepali Prime Minster Balendra Shah called the disaster "unimaginable and heartbreaking."

items.title: CIA-backed investor helped top German drones firm break into US
items.summary: MUNICH: German drone maker Quantum Systems gained an early foothold in the United States with help from CIA-linked investor In-Q-Tel (IQT), its co-CEO said, highlighting how US capital and networks continue to shape Europe's emerging defence companies. Sven Kruck told Reuters that US investors including IQT helped open doors in Washington and win work with the Central Intelligence Agency and Federal Bureau of Investigation. The company is now one of Europe's biggest defence startups, valued at around US$8 billion.

items.title: From midnight to noon, Hospital Tunku Azizah welcomes 12 Merdeka babies including twin girls
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — As the nation celebrated its 69th National Day, 12 newborns, including a pair of twin girls, began their life stories at Hospital Tunku Azizah (HTA) here today. All ten ‘Merdeka babies’ were delivered between midnight and noon, comprising six baby boys and six baby girls. HTA director Dr Shamsul Anuar Kamarudin said a birth on National Day is not only a special date, but it also carries a deeper meaning as a symbol of life, hope and the nation’s future.

items.title: Lawyer seeks reduced sentence for Malaysian fraud victim jailed in Japan
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The lawyer appointed by the family of a 24-year-old Malaysian sentenced to four years in prison in Japan will travel to the country again to attend an appeal hearing seeking a reduction of his sentence. Lawyer Datuk Noor Svetlana Mohd Noor Nordin said the notice of appeal was filed immediately after Muhammad Faiq Zafran Mohd Jailani was sentenced, on the grounds that he was himself a victim of an online fraud syndicate. She said the appeal would be heard on Sept 8 and handled by a legal aid lawyer at the Nagoya High Court in Kanagawa.

items.title: Tour bus carrying 35 students crashes in Kota Belud, nine hurt
items.summary: KOTA BELUD: Nine students from SM Sains Tuaran suffered minor injuries after a tour bus carrying the school group was involved in an accident at the Jalan Kota Belud-Kundasang junction today. "Upon arriving at 11.40am, we found that the accident involved a tour bus carrying students from SM Sains Tuaran. "Nine students were reported to have suffered minor injuries and were taken to Kota Belud Hospital for treatment," he said when contacted.

items.title: Nine students injured after school bus carrying 36 crashes in Sabah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — Nine students from Sekolah Menengah (SM) Sains Sabah suffered minor injuries after a bus carrying 35 students and a teacher was involved in an accident on the Kota Belud-Kundasang road in Sabah this morning. Kota Belud Fire and Rescue Station chief Elge Bakuk said firefighters were dispatched to the scene after receiving an emergency call. “All the victims were later taken to Kota Belud Hospital for further treatment using ambulances from the Health Ministry in Tuaran and Kota Belud, as well as an ambulance from the Malaysian Civil Defence Force,” he said.

items.title: Customs sniffer dogs Goku and Cafrey join military K9s marching at Putrajaya National Day
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 31 — While their daily routine involves tracking drugs at national entry points or performing military guard duty, K9 dogs Goku and Troy share a common mission today, namely marching alongside 33 other dogs at the National Day parade in Dataran Putrajaya. Johnson Pedro said that initial training for the parade involved walking the dogs individually before pairing them with compatible dogs to march side by side. “Military dogs are highly trained.

items.title: Suspect arrested after teen shot when hunting companion mistakes him for animal in Sarawak
items.summary: MIRI, Aug 31 — The shooting case involving a 17-year-old teenager in Long Lidong, Lawas, has been resolved with the arrest of a suspect on August 25, said Lawas district police chief DSP Liong Tindan. Liong said following the arrest of the suspect, the police also recovered a homemade firearm, locally known as a ‘ bakakuk ’, believed to have been used in the incident. “The police are continuing investigations, including tracing witnesses and gathering other information related to the case.

items.title: Kuskop to expedite disbursement of PM’s additional RM1b microcredit pledge, says minister
items.summary: SERDANG, Aug 31 — The Ministry of Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives (Kuskop) will expedite the disbursement of an additional RM1 billion in microcredit funds to micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), following Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s announcement yesterday. Minister Steven Sim said the increase in allocation brings this year’s total microcredit funding to RM6 billion, up from RM5 billion. Yesterday, Anwar, who is also finance minister, announced the additional RM1 billion in micro financing facilities and said the government had agreed to raise the e-invoice exemption threshold from RM1 million to RM3 million annually.

items.title: Election Commission to reveal proposed new, renamed Sarawak state seats on Sept 1
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 31 — The names and locations of Sarawak’s 17 proposed new State Legislative Assembly (DUN) constituencies will finally be publicly unveiled by the Election Commission (EC) tomorrow (September 1). The announcement is eagerly anticipated as it will provide greater clarity on the proposed expansion of the Sarawak Legislative Assembly from 82 to 99 seats, following the redelineation exercise undertaken by the EC. Apart from the new seats, the EC has proposed renaming several existing seats.

items.title: Penang council seizes licensed dog after viral video shows attack on stray in Tanjung Bungah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — Penang authorities have seized a licensed dog after a viral video showed it repeatedly attacking a smaller stray in Tanjung Bungah, with the incident now under investigation under the Animal Welfare Act 2015. According to The Star , the Penang Island City Council (MBPP) said it seized the dog today after receiving a complaint through its official WhatsApp channel yesterday over the incident at Pearl Hill. MBPP said checks found that the dog had a valid licence and was registered as a mixed breed.

items.title: ‘Ultraman’ detained near main stage ahead of Sultan Nazrin’s arrival at Perak National Day celebration, says state police chief
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — A man dressed as Ultraman was detained near the main stage at Perak’s National Day celebrations today after police said his behaviour appeared suspicious in an area where Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah and other members of the Perak royal family were due to be seated. According to Berita Harian , Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the local man, who is in his 40s, was detained at about 5am after he was seen entering and lingering near the main stage area. Also present were Raja Muda Perak Raja Jaafar Raja Muda Musa, Raja Di Hilir Perak Raja Iskandar Dzulkarnain Idris Shah, Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad and members of the state executive council.

items.title: Malaysia Day 2026: Final prep meeting set for Sept 5 ahead of Kuching celebration, says Fahmi
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 31 — A meeting to review the final preparations for the 2026 Malaysia Day celebration in Kuching, Sarawak, will be held on September 5, ahead of the main event at the Borneo Convention Centre Kuching (BCCK) on September 16. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the official celebration would take place on the night of September 16, with various side events lined up around BCCK and Plaza Merdeka to enliven the Malaysia Day festivities. Fahmi, who is also chairman of the 2026 National Day and Malaysia Day (HKHM) main committee, said he was confident that Malaysians from across the country would attend the event, which would feature an exhibition tracing the history of Malaysia’s formation.

items.title: ‘Habis madu, sepah dibuang’: Anthony Loke posts Malay proverb after Ong Kian Ming quits DAP
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke today posted a Malay proverb on Facebook shortly after former Bangi MP Ong Kian Ming announced his resignation from the party after 14 years. “ Habis madu, sepah dibuang ,” Loke wrote in the brief post. Ong announced earlier today that his resignation from DAP would take effect today, bringing to an end his membership of the party since 2012.

items.title: Voice behind National Day air show, Major Dinnesh brings fighter jet manoeuvres alive
items.summary: The role of air show commentator, says Dinnesh, a 34-year-old Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) officer, goes far beyond reading a script into a microphone. “That was where my career as an air show commentator with the RMAF began,” said the officer, who now serves in the RMAF Air Defence Control Division, in an interview with Bernama. For the 2026 National Day parade and march-past, Dinnesh took on the role of air commentator alongside Major Neny Suhaida Ab Suki and Captain Muhammad Iqbal Nasrudin.

items.title: Roar of fighter jets dominates Putrajaya skies as RMAF stages National Day air show
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 31 — The roar of fighter jets reverberated across the skies over Putrajaya today as the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) staged a thrilling air display, one of the highlights of the 69th National Day celebration. Royal Malaysian Air Force chief General Tan Sri Muhamad Norazlan Aris once again took to the cockpit of a Sukhoi Su-30MKM to lead the display, marking the second consecutive year he has personally led the National Day air show. Four Su-30MKMs, four F/A-18D Hornets and three BAE Hawk 208 fighter jets thundered across the skies, showcasing the nation’s air capabilities and operational readiness.

items.title: Malaysia’s King and Queen mark 69th National Day, send greetings to all citizens
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — Malaysia’s King and Queen, Their Majesties Sultan Ibrahim and Raja Zarith Sofiah, extended 69th National Day greetings to all Malaysians. The royal message was conveyed through a post on Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar’s official Facebook page today. Earlier, Their Majesties arrived at the National Day celebration in Putrajaya at 8am and were received by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his wife, Datuk Seri Dr. Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, as well as Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, who also serves as chairman of the National Day and Malaysia Day (HKHM) 2026 Main Committee.

items.title: Sarawak to carry out cloud seeding Sept 3 to 5 as haze worsens, four water plants shut
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — Sarawak will carry out cloud seeding from September 3 to 5 as authorities grapple with worsening haze and critically low reservoir levels that have already forced four water treatment plants to stop operating. According to Harian Metro , Sarawak Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas said the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) expected conditions to be suitable for the operation during the three-day window. Uggah, who chairs the committee, said the Rural Water Supply Department had reported that four water treatment plants had been forced to suspend operations because reservoir levels had fallen too low.

items.title: Sarawak says no emergency unless API breaches 500, Serian readings remain hazardous
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 31 — A state of emergency will only be declared if the Air Pollutant Index (API) reaches 500 or above under the National Haze Action Plan, said Sarawak Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas. The Sarawak Disaster Management Committee (SDMC) chairman clarified that there is currently no necessity to declare a state of emergency yet. Both readings remain within the hazardous level.

items.title: National Day reflections: Zahid stresses TVET jobs, Fadillah calls for harmony and shared future
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — The meaning of independence must be reflected in people’s lives by ensuring they have access to skills, better employment opportunities and are not left behind in the nation’s development, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said. Ahmad Zahid said the struggle today was no longer about achieving independence, but ensuring that its true meaning remained alive in the lives of the people. He said independence should also create opportunities for small entrepreneurs to grow and enable every family to improve their lives.

items.title: ‘Not today’: Gobind keeps politics off the table on National Day as questions turn to Ong Kian Ming’s DAP resignation
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 31 — DAP national chairman Gobind Singh Deo today declined to comment on former Bangi MP Ong Kian Ming’s resignation from the party, saying National Day was not the time for politics. According to the New Straits Times , Gobind said he had yet to read Ong’s statement and deferred any response to another time. No politics today.

items.title: ‘Great show!’ Anwar thanks Malaysians, mingles with crowds at National Day parade
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 31 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim praised and expressed his appreciation to everyone involved, as well as members of the public who attended the 2026 National Day celebration at Dataran Putrajaya here today. “Great, great show! One member of the crowd even thanked the Prime Minister for restoring the monthly basic eligibility quota under the Budi Madani RON95 (Budi95) programme from 200 litres to 300 litres, which he announced during the National Day Prime Minister’s Address yesterday.

items.title: Putrajaya’s free water taxis become crowd favourite, offering scenic shortcut to National Day venue
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 31 — The free water taxi service emerged as a highlight for visitors at the 2026 National Day celebration in Dataran Putrajaya today, with people from all walks of life seizing the opportunity to cross Putrajaya Lake in a spirit of patriotism. Route 1 runs from the Terra 8 Jetty, Presint 8, to the Monument Jetty, Presint 2, while Route 2 connects the Putrajaya Lake Club Jetty to the Monument Jetty, Presint 2. Route 3 operates between the Putrajaya Marina Jetty, Presint 5, and the Anjung Floria Jetty, Presint 4.

items.title: Upin & Ipin, police dogs and fighter jets steal the show at Malaysia’s 69th National Day parade
items.summary: His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, and Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, Queen of Malaysia, attend National Day 2026 celebrations at Dataran Putrajaya in Putrajaya on August 31, 2026. People attend National Day 2026 celebrations at Dataran Putrajaya in Putrajaya on August 31, 2026.

items.title: Twenty‑three injured after tour bus crashes at Kanowit roundabout along Pan Borneo Highway
items.summary: SIBU, Aug 31 — Twenty-three people were injured after a tour bus was involved in a single-vehicle accident at the Kanowit roundabout along the Pan Borneo Highway here early Monday. A statement from the Sarawak Fire and Rescue Department (Bomba) operations centre said it received a distress call at 2.25am and deployed six firefighters from the Sibu Jaya fire station to the scene. It said the injured victims received initial treatment from medical personnel before being taken to Sibu Hospital and Kanowit Hospital for further treatment.

items.title: ‘Harsh, but true’: Kedah MB stands by gambling remarks, denies targeting Anwar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor has stood by his controversial remarks over gambling, saying that although his words were harsh, they were directed at gambling interests and not Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. “I targeted the gambling tycoons.
